facts.statement: Richard Owen named and described the dinosaur Scelidosaurus in 1859.
facts.quote: After initial finds in the 1850s, comparative anatomist Richard Owen named and described Scelidosaurus in 1859.

facts.statement: Only one species, Scelidosaurus harrisonii, is currently considered valid, though another was proposed in 1996.
facts.quote: Only one species, Scelidosaurus harrisonii named by Owen in 1861, is considered valid today, although one other species was proposed in 1996.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus lived approximately 191 million years ago during the Early Jurassic epoch.
facts.quote: Scelidosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic epoch, during the Sinemurian to Pliensbachian ages around 191 million years ago

facts.statement: Fossils of Scelidosaurus have been found in the Charmouth Mudstone Formation near Charmouth in Dorset, England.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found in the Charmouth Mudstone Formation near Charmouth in Dorset, England

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus was approximately 4 meters long.
facts.quote: Scelidosaurus was about 4 m long.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus was largely quadrupedal and fed on low scrubby plants.
facts.quote: It was a largely quadrupedal animal, feeding on low scrubby plants

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus was lightly armored with long horizontal rows of keeled oval scutes running along its neck, back, and tail.
facts.quote: Scelidosaurus was lightly armoured, protected by long horizontal rows of keeled oval scutes that stretched along the neck, back and tail.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Scelidosaurus weighed 270 kg and measured 3.8 meters in length in 2010.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul gave a body length of 3.8 metres (12.5 ft) and a weight of 270 kg.

facts.statement: The premaxillae of Scelidosaurus bore a small upper beak in life.
facts.quote: The front snout bones, the premaxillae, have a common central rough extension, in life bearing a small upper beak.

facts.statement: The snout of Scelidosaurus, largely formed by nasal bones, was flat on top.
facts.quote: The snout, largely formed by the nasal bones, was flat on top.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus had very large, conspicuous round openings in the top of its rear skull that served as attachment points for powerful jaw-closing muscles.
facts.quote: The upper temporal fenestrae were very large, forming conspicuous round openings in the top of the rear skull, serving as attachment areas for the powerful muscles that closed the lower jaws.

facts.statement: Fine ridges on the frontal bones of Scelidosaurus indicate the presence of keratinous plates, similar to modern turtles.
facts.quote: The frontal bones were covered by a halo of fine ridges; these indicate the presence of keratinous plates, as with modern turtles.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus had at least five teeth in each premaxilla, nineteen in the maxilla, and sixteen in the lower jaw dentary.
facts.quote: There were at least five teeth in each premaxilla, and at least nineteen in the maxilla and sixteen in the dentary of the lower jaw.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus is a genus of herbivorous, armored ornithischian dinosaur from the Jurassic of England.
facts.quote: Scelidosaurus (; with the intended meaning of "limb lizard", from Greek /σκελίς meaning 'rib of beef' and sauros/σαυρος meaning 'lizard') is a genus of herbivorous armoured ornithischian dinosaur from the Jurassic of England.

facts.statement: The exact placement of Scelidosaurus within the thyreophoran group has been debated for nearly 150 years.
facts.quote: One of the oldest known and most "primitive" of the thyreophorans, the exact placement of Scelidosaurus within this group has been the subject of debate for nearly 150 years.

facts.statement: Current evidence suggests Scelidosaurus is a derived basal thyreophoran closely related to either Ankylosauria or Stegosauria+Ankylosauria.
facts.quote: Today most evidence suggests that Scelidosaurus is the most derived of the known basal thyreophorans, either closely related to Ankylosauria or Stegosauria+Ankylosauria.

facts.statement: In 2020, Norman identified unique bones covering the nasal cavity roof called "epivomers," which are not known from any other animal.
facts.quote: These elements had been sketched by Norman in the seventies prior to the incident and interpreted as parts of the pterygoids, but in 2020 he concluded that they were special bones covering the roof of the nasal cavity, which he named the "epivomers". These are not known from any other animal.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus had a torso that was relatively flat in side view and taller than wide, unlike the extremely vertically compressed bodies of ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: The torso was relatively flat in side view, however, despite the belly being broad, it was not extremely vertically compressed as with ankylosaurs but taller than wide.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus had a relatively short, quickly tapering tail that likely represented about half of its total body length.
facts.quote: The quickly tapering tail was relatively short, probably representing about half of body length.

facts.statement: The coracoid bone of Scelidosaurus was circular in side view.
facts.quote: The coracoid was circular in side view.

facts.statement: The claws of Scelidosaurus were flat, hoof-shaped, and curved inward.
facts.quote: The claws were flat, hoof-shaped and curved to the inside.

facts.statement: The most obvious feature of Scelidosaurus is its armor, which consisted of bony scutes embedded in the skin.
facts.quote: The most obvious feature of Scelidosaurus is its armour, consisting of bony scutes embedded in the skin.

facts.statement: The skull of Scelidosaurus featured bony outgrowths covering much of its surface, along with separate bony plates that formed a pair of horns extending upward and backward from the rear.
facts.quote: The skull consists of bony outgrowths covering much of its surface, accompanied by separate bony plates encircling the upper portion of the eye socket and forming a pair of horns that extend upward and backward from the rear of the skull.

facts.statement: The top neck rows of Scelidosaurus included a pair of unique three-pointed scutes located directly behind the head.
facts.quote: The first osteoderms of the top neck rows formed a pair of unique three-pointed scutes directly behind the head.

facts.statement: Compared to later ankylosaurs, Scelidosaurus was lightly armored, lacking continuous plating, spikes, or a pelvic shield.
facts.quote: Compared to the later Ankylosauria, Scelidosaurus was lightly armoured, without continuous plating, spikes or pelvic shield.

facts.statement: Between its bony scutes, Scelidosaurus had rounded, non-overlapping scales similar to those of the modern Gila monster.
facts.quote: Between the bony scutes, Scelidosaurus had rounded non-overlapping scales like the present Gila monster.

facts.statement: Very small, flat bone granules measuring 5-10 millimeters were perhaps distributed within the skin between the large scutes of Scelidosaurus.
facts.quote: Between the large scutes, very small (5-10 millimetres [0.2-0.4 in]) flat "granules" of bone were perhaps distributed within the skin.

facts.statement: Some recent specimens of Scelidosaurus show osteoderms with keels shaped like thorns or spikes.
facts.quote: Some of the latest specimens found show partly different osteoderms including scutes on which the keel is more like a thorn or spike.

facts.statement: Fossilized skin impressions have been found for Scelidosaurus.
facts.quote: Fossilized skin impressions have also been found.

facts.statement: The osteoderms of Scelidosaurus varied in size and shape, with most being oval plates featuring a high keel on the outside where the highest point was positioned toward the rear.
facts.quote: The osteoderms of Scelidosaurus ranged in both size and shape. Most were smaller or larger oval plates with a high keel on the outside, the highest point of the keel positioned more to the rear.

facts.statement: James Harrison discovered Scelidosaurus fossils in the Black Ven cliffs of Charmouth, West Dorset, England during the 1850s.
facts.quote: During the 1850s, quarry owner James Harrison of Charmouth, West Dorset of England found fossils from the cliffs of Black Ven between Charmouth and Lyme Regis

facts.statement: Richard Owen named the genus Scelidosaurus in 1859 within an entry for the Encyclopædia Britannica.
facts.quote: In 1859, Owen named the genus Scelidosaurus in an entry about palaeontology in the Encyclopædia Britannica

facts.statement: Richard Owen originally intended to name the dinosaur "hindlimb saurian" but mistakenly used a Greek word meaning "rib of beef" instead of "hindlimb".
facts.quote: Owen intended to call the dinosaur "hindlimb saurian" but confused the Greek word σκέλος, , "hindlimb", with σκελίς, , "rib of beef".

facts.statement: Richard Owen described a nearly complete skeleton of Scelidosaurus in 1863, which included a skull previously thought to be separate.
facts.quote: The skull later was revealed to be part of a nearly complete skeleton, that was described by Owen in 1863

facts.statement: In 1888, Richard Lydekker designated a knee joint specimen (NHMUK PV 39496) as the type specimen for Scelidosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1888, Richard Lydekker while cataloguing the NHMUK fossils, designated some of the hindlimb fragments described in 1861, specimen NHMUK PV 39496 consisting of a lower part of a femur and an upper part of the tibia and fibula, together forming a knee joint, as the type specimen

facts.statement: Bernard Newman discovered in 1968 that the knee joint originally selected as the type specimen actually belonged to a theropod dinosaur, not Scelidosaurus.
facts.quote: this was not discovered until 1968 by Bernard Newman

facts.statement: The International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature established in 1994 that specimen NHMUK PV R 1111 is the lectotype of Scelidosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1994 the ICZN reacted positively, in Opinion 1788 deciding that the skull and skeleton, specimen NHMUK PV R 1111, would be the new lectotype of Scelidosaurus

facts.statement: The lectotype skeleton of Scelidosaurus was found in marine deposits dating to the late Sinemurian stage, approximately 191 million years ago.
facts.quote: The new lectotype skeleton had been uncovered in the Black Ven Marl or Woodstone Nodule Bed, marine deposits of the Charmouth Mudstone Formation, dating from the late Sinemurian stage, about 191 million years ago

facts.statement: The lectotype skeleton of Scelidosaurus is nearly complete, missing only the snout tip, neck base, forelimbs, and tail end.
facts.quote: Only the snout tip, the neck base, the forelimbs and the tail end are missing

facts.statement: Hundreds of osteoderms were found associated with the Scelidosaurus skeleton, many remaining in their original positions.
facts.quote: Hundreds of osteoderms were found in connection with the skeleton, many more or less in their original position

facts.statement: David Bruce Norman published new descriptions of the Scelidosaurus skull and postcrania in 2020, incorporating later findings.
facts.quote: In 2020, Norman published articles on the skull and the postcrania, also taking later finds into account

facts.statement: Acid bath treatments used to prepare the Scelidosaurus fossils caused severe deterioration, breakage, and crumbling of the bones due to leakages.
facts.quote: It transpired that the acid baths had, through leakages, severely deteriorated the condition of the bones, further mishandling leading to breakage and crumbling

facts.statement: Richard Owen hypothesized in 1861 that Scelidosaurus was a fish-eater that partially lived in the sea, a view that differs from modern interpretations.
facts.quote: Owen in 1861 suggested a lifestyle for Scelidosaurus that is very different from present ideas: it would have been a fish-eater and partially sea-dwelling

facts.statement: It is debated whether the misidentified knee joint specimen belongs to Scelidosaurus or to a member of the Coelophysoidea or Neoceratosauria.
facts.quote: It more likely belongs to some member of the Coelophysoidea or Neoceratosauria

facts.statement: The original left thighbone (GSM 109560) sent to Richard Owen was determined to belong to a theropod dinosaur, not Scelidosaurus.
facts.quote: The original left thighbone, GSM 109560, belonged to a theropod

facts.statement: In 1888, R. Lydekker cataloged numerous single bones, mostly limb elements and osteoderms, acquired by the Natural History Museum, London, from the Norris collection.
facts.quote: In 1888 Lydekker catalogued a large number of single bones, largely limb elements, and osteoderms, that had been acquired by the NHMUK from the Norris collection.

facts.statement: In 1861, Richard Owen described a second partial juvenile skeleton, now registered as specimen LYMPH 1997.37.4-10 in the Lyme Regis Museum.
facts.quote: Owen in 1861 described a second, partial, skeleton of a juvenile animal, that later was added to the collection of Elizabeth Philpot and today is registered in the Lyme Regis Museum as specimen LYMPH 1997.37.4-10.

facts.statement: Richard Owen speculated that Scelidosaurus might have been ovoviviparous based on its relatively large size and presumed marine lifestyle.
facts.quote: As it was relatively large, Owen speculated, in the context of its presumed marine lifestyle, that Scelidosaurus might have been ovoviviparous.

facts.statement: A second partial juvenile skeleton, specimen NHMUK PV R6704, was described in 1968 after being reported in 1959.
facts.quote: In 1968 a second partial juvenile skeleton was described, specimen NHMUK PV R6704, that had already been reported in 1959.

facts.statement: In 1985, Simon Barnsley, David Costain, and Peter Langham excavated a partial skeleton with a complete skull and skin impressions, now registered as specimen BRSMG CE12785 at the Bristol Museum.
facts.quote: In 1985 Simon Barnsley, David Costain and Peter Langham excavated a partial skeleton including a very complete skull and skin impressions, which was sold to the Bristol Museum where it is registered as specimen BRSMG CE12785.

facts.statement: Between 1980 and 2000, palaeontologist Roger Byrne discovered three fossils on a beach near The Gobbins in Northern Ireland.
facts.quote: Between the years 1980 and 2000, three fossils were discovered on a beach near The Gobbins in Northern Ireland by palaeontologist Roger Byrne.

facts.statement: Histologist Robin Reid identified the first specimen as dinosaurian in 1989 based on bone texture and structure, suspecting it belonged to Scelidosaurus or a similar animal.
facts.quote: Histologist Robin Reid recognized the first specimen as dinosaurian due to its bone texture and structure, and reported it in 1989, suspecting it belonged to Scelidosaurus or a similar animal.

facts.statement: Researchers concluded that the osteoderms of all basal armored dinosaurs were covered in a tough, likely keratinous layer of skin.
facts.quote: The authors concluded that the osteoderms of all basal armoured dinosaurs were covered in a tough, probably keratinous layer of skin.

facts.statement: Although fragmentary fossils led to a reassessment placing S. oehleri in Scelidosaurus, this view was not accepted, and it is now recognized as Tatisaurus.
facts.quote: Although the fossils are fragmentary, this reassessment has not been accepted, and S. oehleri is today once again recognized as Tatisaurus.

facts.statement: In 2016, Peter Malcolm Galton and Kenneth Carpenter identified the Arizona specimens as a nomen dubium, placing them as Thyreophora indet.
facts.quote: In 2016, Peter Malcolm Galton and Kenneth Carpenter identified it as a nomen dubium, instead once again placing the specimens as Thyreophora indet.

facts.statement: Sir Richard Owen classified Scelidosaurus within the Dinosauria in 1861.
facts.quote: Scelidosaurus was placed in the Dinosauria by Owen in 1861.

facts.statement: Sir Richard Owen described Scelidosaurus in 1859 following initial fossil finds in the 1850s.
facts.quote: Después de los hallazgos iniciales en la década de 1850, el anatomista comparativo Sir Richard Owen describió a Scelidosaurus en 1859.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus lived approximately 196 to 183 million years ago during the Early Jurassic in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: vivió a principios del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 196 y 183 millones años, desde el Sinemuriense hasta el Pliensbachiense, en lo que hoy es Europa.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus and related genera lived on the supercontinent Laurasia during the Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: Este género y los otros relacionados de ese momento vivían en el supercontinente Laurasia.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus was a lightly armored, quadrupedal herbivore reaching about 4 meters in length.
facts.quote: Era un herbívoro cuadrúpedo, ligeramente acorazado que alcanzaba los 4 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus was relatively small compared to most dinosaurs but represented a medium-sized species for the Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: Un Scelidosaurus totalmente crecido era más bien pequeño, comparado con la mayoría de otros dinosaurios, pero era una especie de tamaño mediano en el Jurásico temprano.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Scelidosaurus to be 3.8 meters long and weigh 270 kilograms in 2010.
facts.quote: En 2010, Gregory S. Paul dio una longitud corporal de 3,8 metros (12,5 pies) y un peso de 270 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus was quadrupedal with hind limbs considerably longer than the forelimbs.
facts.quote: Scelidosaurus era cuadrúpedo, con los miembros traseros considerablemente más largos que los delanteros.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus had four toes on each foot, with the inner digit being the smallest.
facts.quote: Scelidosaurus tenía cuatro dedos en cada pie, siendo el dígito interior el más pequeño.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus possessed light armor consisting of long horizontal rows of keeled oval shields extending along the neck, back, and tail.
facts.quote: Scelidosaurus tenía una armadura ligera, protegido por largas filas horizontales de escudos ovalados con quillas que se extendían a lo largo del cuello, lomo y cola.

facts.statement: David Norman concluded Scelidosaurus fed on low scrubby vegetation up to one meter in height.
facts.quote: Norman concluded that Scelidosaurus fed on low scrubby vegetation, with a height up to one metre.

facts.statement: Pollen evidence suggests conifers of the extinct family Cheirolepidiaceae grew on the Early Jurassic islands of Europe where Scelidosaurus lived.
facts.quote: The presence of Classopolis pollen in the sediments suggests that conifers belonging to the extinct family Cheirolepidiaceae grew on the islands.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the family Scelidosauridae is paraphyletic or monophyletic, with Benton (2004) arguing for the latter.
facts.quote: Today, paleontologists usually consider the Scelidosauridae paraphyletic, thus not forming a separate branch or clade; however, Benton (2004) lists the group as monophyletic.

facts.statement: The exact phylogenetic position of Scelidosaurus remains debated, with some viewing it as a true ankylosaur and others as basal to the ankylosaur-stegosaur split.
facts.quote: This debate is still ongoing; at this time, Scelidosaurus is considered to be either more closely related to ankylosaurids than to stegosaurids and, by extension, a true ankylosaur, or basal to the ankylosaur-stegosaur split.

facts.statement: The precise placement of Scelidosaurus within the suborder Thyreophora has been debated for nearly 150 years.
facts.quote: Al ser uno de los tireofóros más primitivos, la ubicación exacta de Scelidosaurus dentro del suborden ha sido un tema de debate por cerca de 150 años.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus has been called the first complete dinosaur, a claim also made for Compsognathus.
facts.quote: Scelidosaurus ha sido llamado el primer dinosaurio completo, aunque lo mismo ha sido reclamado para Compsognathus.

facts.statement: A trackway from the Holy Cross Mountains in Poland shows a Scelidosaurus-like animal walking bipedally, suggesting it may have been more competent at bipedalism than previously thought.
facts.quote: Un sendero de las montañas Holy Cross de Polonia muestra un animal parecido a un Scelidosaurus caminando de manera bípeda, lo que sugiere que pudo haber sido más competente en el bipedalismo de lo que se pensaba anteriormente.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus had a low, triangular skull that was longer than it was wide, resembling early ornithischians rather than later ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: A diferencia de los anquilosaurianos posteriores, el cráneo tenía una forma baja y triangular, más largo que ancho, similar al de los primeros ornitisquios.

facts.statement: The head of Scelidosaurus was small, measuring about 20 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: La cabeza de Scelidosaurus era pequeña, de unos 20 centímetros de largo y alargada.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus was a herbivore with small, leaf-shaped molar teeth suitable for shredding vegetation.
facts.quote: Como otros tireóforos, Scelidosaurus era herbívoro, con los dientes malares muy pequeños, foliformes convenientes para desmenuzar la vegetación.

facts.statement: The large upper temporal fenestrae formed round openings on the back of the skull that served as attachment points for powerful jaw-closing muscles.
facts.quote: Las fenestras temporales superiores eran muy grandes y formaban orificios redondos visibles en la parte superior del cráneo posterior, que servían como áreas de unión para los poderosos músculos que cerraban las mandíbulas inferiores.

facts.statement: In 2020, Norman concluded that a specific brow bone was a fused palpebral bone.
facts.quote: En 2020, Norman concluyó que se trataba de un hueso palpebral fusionado.

facts.statement: Specialized bones called epivomers, found on the roof of the nasal cavity, are known from no other animal.
facts.quote: No se conocen de ningún otro animal.

facts.statement: The vertebral column of Scelidosaurus contained at least 6 cervical, 17 dorsal, 4 sacral, and at least 35 caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: La columna vertebral de Scelidosaurus contenía al menos 6 vértebras del cuello, 17 vértebras dorsales, 4 vértebras sacras y al menos 35 vértebras de la cola.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus had a relatively flat torso that was taller than it was wide, unlike the vertically compressed bodies of later ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: El torso era relativamente plano en la vista lateral, sin embargo, a pesar de que el vientre era ancho, no estaba extremadamente comprimido verticalmente como en los anquilosaurios, sino más alto que ancho.

facts.statement: The tail was relatively short, tapering quickly to represent approximately half the total body length.
facts.quote: La cola que se estrechaba rápidamente era relativamente corta, probablemente representando aproximadamente la mitad de la longitud del cuerpo.

facts.statement: The hip area and the base of the tail were rigidified by a large amount of ossified tendons.
facts.quote: El área de la cadera y la base de la cola estaban rígidas por una gran cantidad de tendones osificados.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus possessed flat, hoof-shaped claws that curved inward.
facts.quote: Las garras eran planas, con forma de pezuña y curvadas hacia el interior.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus had four large toes, with the innermost toe being the smallest.
facts.quote: Scelidosaurus tenía cuatro dedos grandes, siendo el dedo más interno el más pequeño.

facts.statement: The fourth toe was long and constructed to extend outward to improve stability, despite having a short metatarsal bone.
facts.quote: El cuarto metatarsiano era corto pero su dedo era largo y estaba construido para extenderse hacia el exterior del pie, para mejorar la estabilidad.

facts.statement: Researchers believe Scelidosaurus fed by crushing food between its teeth using a simple up-and-down jaw movement.
facts.quote: Se cree Scelidosaurus se alimentaba con sistema de en el que el alimento entre los dientes era machacado con un movimiento de arriba abajo simple de las quijadas.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus is most famous for its armor made of bony shields embedded in its skin.
facts.quote: La característica más obvia de Scelidosaurus es su armadura, que consiste de escudos óseos incrustados en la piel.

facts.statement: The animal's osteoderms were arranged in parallel strips running from the neck to the tail on both sides of its body.
facts.quote: Estos osteodermos se disponían en franjas paralelas a ambos lados del animal recorriendo desde el cuello a la cola.

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus is distinguished from Scutellosaurus by its conical side shields rather than sharp osteoderms.
facts.quote: Los escudos laterales eran cónicos, a diferencia de los osteodermos afilados de Scutellosaurus, y se han utilizado para identificar el género.

facts.statement: The animal possessed a pair of distinctive three-pointed shields located directly behind its head.
facts.quote: También tenía un par de escudos distintivos de tres puntas detrás de la cabeza.

facts.statement: Between the main rows of armor, Scelidosaurus had one or two rows of smaller, keeled oval shields.
facts.quote: Entre estas series principales, estaban presentes una o dos filas de escudos de quillas ovaladas más pequeñas.

facts.statement: The tail featured four rows of large shields: one on the upper midline, one on the lower midline, and one on each side.
facts.quote: Había en total cuatro filas de escudos grandes en la cola, una en la línea media superior, una en la línea media de la parte inferior y una en cada lado de la cola.

facts.statement: Two rows of large shields ran along each side of the neck.
facts.quote: El cuello tenía a cada lado dos filas de grandes escudos.

facts.statement: The lower row of neck osteoderms were very large, flat, and plate-like.
facts.quote: Los osteodermos de la fila inferior del cuello eran muy grandes, planos y en forma de placa.

facts.statement: The top row of neck osteoderms formed a unique pair of three-pointed shields situated just behind the head.
facts.quote: Los primeros osteodermos de las filas superiores del cuello formaron un par de escudos únicos de tres puntas directamente detrás de la cabeza.

facts.statement: The shields were generally largest at the front of the torso and decreased in size towards the rear, particularly on the thigh surface.
facts.quote: En general, los escudos eran más grandes en la parte delantera del torso y los osteodermos disminuían hacia la parte posterior, especialmente en la superficie de los muslos.

facts.statement: Compared to later Ankylosaurians, Scelidosaurus was lightly armored, lacking continuous plates, spikes, or a pelvic shield.
facts.quote: Comparado con los miembros de Ankylosauria, Scelidosaurus estaba ligeramente blindado, sin placas continuas, púas o escudo pélvico.

facts.statement: Fossilized skin impressions show that Scelidosaurus had rounded scales similar to those of a Gila monster between its bony shields.
facts.quote: Las impresiones fosilizadas de la piel también se han encontrado. Entre los escudos óseos, Scelidosaurus tenía escamas redondeadas similares a las de un monstruo de Gila.

facts.statement: Very small, flat bone granules measuring 5 to 10 millimeters were distributed within the skin between the large shields.
facts.quote: Entre los escudos grandes, muy pequeños gránulos planos de entre 5 a 10 milímetros de hueso estaban distribuidos dentro de la piel.

facts.statement: Some recent specimens show partially different osteoderms, including shields where the keel resembles a spine.
facts.quote: Algunos de los últimos especímenes encontrados muestran osteodermos parcialmente diferentes, incluidos escudos en los que la quilla se parece más a una espina.

facts.statement: Some specimens appear to have small horns at the rear corners of the head, positioned on the squamosal bones.
facts.quote: Estos especímenes también parecen tener pequeños cuernos en las esquinas posteriores de la cabeza, colocados en los huesos escamosos.

facts.quote: PBDB name: Scelidosaurus (genus), Owen 1859

facts.quote: Parent group: Scelidosauridae

facts.statement: The family of Scelidosaurus is Scelidosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Scelidosauridae

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Scelidosaurus lived from the Rhaetian to the Toarcian, between 205.7 and 174.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rhaetian to Toarcian (205.7 to 174.7 million years ago)

facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 13
